newsitem.title: USA: Humana Q1 net income hurt by costs, revs up.
newsitem.headline: Humana Q1 net income hurt by costs, revs up.

text.p: Humana Inc said on Tuesday its net income in the first quarter declined to $39 million from $53 million in the same period last year, due to increases in medical and administrative costs.
"This quarter marks the first quarter of sequential earnings improvement in a year, but these results did not come easily," said Gregory Wolf, Humana's president.

Wolf said the company had made progress in eliminating unprofitable business by selling operations, exiting certain markets and pricing products more appropriately, but it faced work implementing improved medical management processes.
First quarter revenues rose 16 percent to $1.8 billion from the same period last year.

Same-store commercial membership decreased 113,400 members during the quarter, Humana said. This decline, which excluded the sale of Humana's Washington, D.C. health plan and the purchase of Health Direct, was due to the company's more disciplined product pricing begun in the fall of 1996 and withdrawal from certain unprofitable markets, it said.
Same-store Medicare risk membership increased 15,100 members in the quarter, compared to a same-store increase of 10,200 members in the first quarter of 1996, it said.

The increase was mostly due to the company's revenues earned from its Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Uniformed Services contract as well as premium rate increases in its commercial and Medicare risk products, Humana said.
